## What this changes

- **The "Report what you found" affordance is wired
  (`web/src/lib/task-page.ts`, `taskReportChannel`).** Two states,
  both honest:
  - **The receiver operates** (`intakeAvailability().operational`):
    the link is the intake form prefilled by a plain GET,
    `/intake/new?task=<handle>` (K11 §5.3). `/intake/` is a live
    service outside the snapshot base (SIG-REL-008), so the href
    joins at the deploy root via `rootPath`, never `withBase`. The
    link renders **only** while `operational` is true — code-enforced
    `false` today (P37.59 / D-P32.16-1), so no form link is ever
    rendered for a receiver that is not operating.
  - **The interim channel (today):** e-mail to the dispute address —
    the same `SIG_DISPUTE_EMAIL`-injected value `/dispute/` names
    (the operator's address until the project contact address exists;
    OP-10, never committed to a file). The block stamps
    `data-intake-email="set|unset"` exactly as `/dispute/` does, and
    names the task handle so the finding lands on the right task.
  - The page **never invents a channel**: an un-operating receiver
    renders no form link, and no address other than the injected one
    can appear.

- **`/task/<handle>/` (`[slug].astro`):** the placeholder sentence
  ("the channel SIG names for it") replaced by the wired block —
  `data-channel="email|intake-form"`, `data-intake-email` marker,
  link `data-testid="task-report-link"`. The per-role "How to act"
  steps (P36.62, K11 §5.3) are unchanged; T1 zero-JS preserved (no
  script added; classification `/task/**` → T1 untouched).

- **`sig.task-page/1` JSON twin (`[handle].json.ts`):** additive
  `how_to_act` (the rendered per-role steps) and `report`
  (`{channel, href, address}`) fields — the same facts the HTML
  renders (HTML = JSON twin parity); schema id unchanged (additive,
  back-compat — the `records_request_draft` precedent).
